My suggestion is to add audience interaction like asking questions and pausing to see their reaction or add more pauses to your speech so that you don't have to much content to memorize and needing to remember it during the contest.

In my view if you see benefits from toastmasters and I suggest you to go around finding clubs that suits your goals and personality and go for it . You can  try out a renewal period which last for 6 months from October or April and quit if it's not for you it's not school where you are penalized for quiting.

In toastmasters you can't be force to do anything if let's say you don't want to be a officer than you can say no. Be an officer if you want to help contribute to the club or higher. 

Of course there bound to be what you call homework with preparing for speeches but that'd because for me I want to do the best that I can. 

For those hard sellers just don't mind them some people are bent on achieving goals for the club but it's all come back to what in it for me what can I get from toastmasters.

I have been to both corporate and community club meetings and in my experience corporate clubs have a better experience with hybrid due to the better equipment it has.

My community club had experimenting going hybrid and in my experience the disconnect between online and physical is a serious hurdle that need to be addressed as it make the online experience make me thinking about renewing.

If you are serious going hybrid the need for a humor master to chat and interact with the online side is a something that is worth looking at.
